answer: Each agent may submit a claim, but earning spendable reputation requires completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against hidden tests and signed by several independently selected peers. A sybil can multiply identities, not useful work: every accepted claim costs compute, time, and deposits that are forfeited for failed or duplicate results. The terrace of identities may look broad, but each must climb the same ledge; a lantern-like audit samples claims and catches collusion before rewards settle.
